correctness.rationale: The specified edge-clock generator is obtained directly from the ab/n, ac/n, bc/n eligible-pair rates. Its fluid drift, martingale bracket, Gaussian fluctuation SDE, uniform-integrability argument and Lyapunov covariance solutions are derived explicitly. The sign numerator has derivative 3(4-y^3)/y^4 and exactly one nontrivial positive root. A symbolic checker reconstructs the Jacobian/noise and proves the covariance ODE exactly; an independent finite-state CTMC checker confirms 12 independent finite-parameter propagations and convergence. The n->infinity claim is proved using martingale FCLT hypotheses, not inferred from finite tests. No claim covers the terminal jamming window.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the closed finite-time cross-part covariance and its one-and-only-one sign change for a naturally balanced tripartite RSA process. Accessible previously documented claims and indexed research were compared at the level of the observable, normalization, and implication. The closest same-graph earlier paper treats first-order fluid matching efficiency; the general CLT methodology is credited. This PASS is best-knowledge only, without independent historical-priority validation, and explicitly retains unavailable-source risks.

value.rationale: Cross-sublattice temporal covariance is a natural observable for multicomponent irreversible dimer deposition. Every accepted event initially removes sites from two components together, while late competition creates anticorrelation. The calculation establishes a unique, parameter-free switch under a fully symmetric deposition rule and supplies an explicit three-mode Gaussian benchmark, which is structurally distinct from a mean coverage formula or a routine finite-state enumeration. A competing earlier same-graph result studies matching efficiency, not the reported second-order observable in its accessible claim.
